title: Uber Stock Slides Nearly 5% After Report Says Alphabet's Waymo Could Walk Away From Their Robotaxi Deal
key_facts: Uber shares fell nearly 5% on Friday 2 Oct 2026 after the Financial Times reported that Waymo is exploring ending its robotaxi partnership with Uber.
Per the FT, citing people familiar, Waymo has held internal talks about ending the deal and has told Uber it plans to enter Austin and Atlanta on its own in January 2028, when the agreement allows.
Uber currently offers Waymo rides through its app in Austin and Atlanta, with Uber managing the fleet with partner Avomo; the Phoenix arrangement ended in June when it expired.
Relations have soured over direct competition, lobbying for different robotaxi rules, and mutual blame over service quality and safety.
Uber has reportedly spent more than 10 billion dollars in the past year on autonomous vehicle investments and fleet deals; Waymo said it has not ruled out a complete split.
Alphabet shares rose 0.58% Friday; Uber shares are down more than 18% this year.
quote_evidence: Waymo has held internal discussions about ending its partnership with Uber and has already informed the ride-hailing company that it plans to enter both cities independently in January 2028, when the current agreement allows, the Financial Times reported, citing people familiar with the matter.
Waymo said it has not ruled out a complete split.
why_it_matters_hint: Uber's robotaxi strategy depends on partners, and its biggest one may walk away.
event_date: FT report and share move on 2 Oct 2026
